pf.license.need: none for shoe or leather repair in most places; the business registration, where the state asks for one
ask: The business registration number, where the state gave one
Proof of business auto insurance, for the van and home visits
pf.license.who: the business; no license for a person
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: a registration the state requires that the owner says the business lacks keeps the business offline
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: liability insurance and cover for customers' shoes while the shop has them, as the business says; shown only once proof is sent
pf.license.otherwise: identity checked, and 'license: what the business says'; customers see no license claim

pf.services.pattern: drop-off: a pair left at the counter, then READY and a pick-up; at a home visit the cobbler looks at the shoes, takes them to the shop and brings them back
pf.services.examples: the example shop's own prices, not a standard

list.name: Heel replacement (pair)
list.place: at the shop; or by a home visit, taken to the shop and brought back

list.name: Boot resole, stitched
list.length: ready in 2 weeks; only with the master cobbler

list.name: Leather and bag repair
list.price: priced from the customer's photos first, or at the counter

list.name: Shoe restoration
list.price: priced at the counter after a look: scuffs, dye, refinishing; written, item by item
list.place: at the shop, or by a home visit

list.name: Fit check
list.price: free, ten minutes at the counter

list.name: Home visit (Lee Mobile Cobbler)
list.price: a $15 pickup fee, credited to the work
list.place: at the customer's home or office
list.before: a card saved for the $15 fee
list.after: Rosie texts the bill after the shoes come back

pf.services.turnaround: days until ready, per service: heels 3 days, half soles 5, a stitched resole 2 weeks; a home visit's shoes come back in about 5 days
pf.services.included: a free fix within 30 days if a sole or a stitch comes loose (not wear and not new damage)
pf.services.capacity: one cobbler at the bench; the stitching machine is used by the master cobbler only
pf.services.nobody_home: no: a home visit needs the customer there to look at the shoes and OK the price; the returned pair is handed to an adult the customer named

before_times: What needs fixing: heels, soles, a zipper, a strap, stretching, or other
The kind of shoe or boot and what it is made of
The date they are needed by
For a home visit: the town and the kind of place
after_time: Anything the cobbler should know, like a favorite pair or a repair done elsewhere
Someone else who may OK the price or pay, like a parent
secure_page_only: A photo of the shoes, if the customer wants to send one
For a home visit: the street address and how to get in
pf.questions.who_may_book: an adult; a parent or guardian books for a child's shoes

pf.safety.stop_action: no danger words of its own: the generic screen (danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency, crisis words) is always on
pf.safety.rated_boots: safety-rated boots (steel toe, electrical hazard): re-soled only with the maker's parts, and the customer is told plainly in writing that the rating can't be promised after any repair; the customer says yes first
pf.safety.medical_shoes: orthopedic or medical shoes: only the outer repair, never the insole, lift or brace; the reason stays on the secure page
pf.safety.during_work: a finding that stops the work, like a sole cracked through or an upper torn through: the work stops, a written note and photo go to the customer, and nothing is charged for what wasn't done
pf.safety.house_calls: a cobbler who feels unsafe at a home leaves, and the owner is told

prep_for_reminder: Bring both shoes of each pair, and any insoles you want kept
For a home visit: have the shoes out, and room to sit and try them on

pf.visit.check_in: the check-in code at the counter; a walk-in drop-off is checked in at the counter at once; at a home visit, the code at the door
pf.visit.intake: a ticket per pair: both shoes photographed, wear and damage noted, the repair asked for, and the date it's needed by; the customer keeps the claim ticket
pf.visit.estimate: written, item by item, before any work; the customer says yes to all, to some items, or not today; good for 7 days
pf.visit.added_work: a new problem found while the shoes are in is texted with its price first; nothing extra without a yes; no answer in 2 days: left as it is
pf.visit.ready: READY texts the pick-up hours, anything due and the held-until date
pf.visit.pick_up: with the claim ticket or the code; a try-on at the counter; handed over once anything due is paid
pf.visit.done_proof: the code at pick-up checks the visit in; at a home visit, DONE after the try-on at the return
pf.visit.claims: a damaged or lost pair is reported within 7 days; the owner decides with the shop's claims policy, never more than the pair's value
pf.visit.unclaimed: pairs not picked up: reminders at 30 and 60 days after READY, then a final written notice with the date before anything is donated at 90 days, as the state's unclaimed-property rules allow; the owner decides
pf.visit.house_call: the cobbler looks at the shoes at the home, prices each item, and takes the pair to the shop; they come back on a booked return, with a try-on

pf.money.before: nothing taken at the shop; a stitched resole takes a $40 deposit that orders the soles; a home visit saves a card for the $15 pickup fee
pf.money.deposit: the $40 resole deposit comes off the price; the rest is paid at pick-up; deposit cap: from the state form
pf.money.after: the rest at the counter at pick-up; for a home visit, the bill Rosie texts after the shoes come back
pf.money.fees: no late-cancel or no-show fee at the shop; at a home visit, the $15 pickup fee for a late cancel or a no-show, only if Sam confirms; it is credited to the work when the work is done
pf.money.materials: special soles, dye or hardware bought for a job are added at cost, with a yes first
pf.money.tax: where the state taxes the work (the owner's setting)

never_in_text: The reason for orthopedic or medical shoes
pf.messages.minors: texts about a child's shoes go to the parent who booked

pf.staff.who_oks: the owner OKs restoration prices over $200, stitched resoles and any fee
pf.staff.stand_in: heels, soles and zippers: any cobbler; stitched resoles and restoration: only the master cobbler

pf.rules.written_price: switch: a written price before work, above an amount: from the state form; the shop writes every item anyway
pf.rules.fees_in_first_price: switch: every required fee, like the pickup fee, inside the first price: from the state form
pf.rules.unclaimed_items: switch: how long finished pairs are held, the written notice, and the waiting time before they're donated or sold: from the state form; the owner decides, and Rosie sends only the notices the owner OKs
pf.rules.right_to_cancel_at_home: switch: a right to cancel work sold at the customer's home: from the state form

notes:
BUILT Oct 27 2026 (P3 new profession D3, REDESIGN 2 master, frozen). No old flowchart or sample plug-in existed (a new profession), so the plug-in is built from the trade's norm. Start: the refitted tailor (from: tailor). Style Drop-off, pattern dropoff.
Why tailor: a cobbler works like a tailor. The pair is looked at, priced item by item in writing, left at the shop, READY, and picked up with a try-on. Flow B is the tailor's shape too: a home visit where the cobbler looks at the shoes and prices them, takes them to the shop, and brings them back on a booked return (own steps B8-x01 and B8-x02).
Facts: dropoff, extrawork. No switches ($2 applies). Settings: arrive A set start, B 2-hour window; cutoff A 24 hours before, B 6pm the day before.
Money A (3 paths): list|none|counter (main: new heels for dress shoes, $35, nothing taken, paid at pick-up), visit|none|counter (boot restoration priced at the counter: boot restoration $110 + sole guard $15 in the example, the customer says yes first), list|deposit|counter (stitched boot resole $140: a $40 deposit orders the soles, the $100 rest at pick-up; the late-cancel fee is the $40 deposit).
Money B (2 paths): visit|card|bill (main: a home visit for boots and dress shoes; only the $15 pickup fee is promised, with a card saved for it; each item priced at the visit: boots $165 + dress shoes $80 = $245; the bill after the shoes come back, the fee credited to the work), list|card|bill (heel replacement $35 by a home visit). The $15 pickup fee is the late-cancel and no-show fee, charged only on Sam's yes. No deposit or full price in flow B.
The master's B numbers become shoe numbers by rename pairs ($89 to $15, $179 to $35, $150 to $55, $199 to $40, $160 to $40, $120 an hour to $60 an hour), so every master line that names a price shows the shop's own.
Licenses: none for shoe or leather repair or for any person; the company gives its business registration only (S1-60 '1 A license' and S2-28 '1 Yes, each one' off, S11-42 license branches off). The second kind of work (leather repair) is registration only too (S1-38 asks 'license or registration only?'). Fake license numbers use EX-1042 style. No state, law or number from one state.
Safety and who must not be booked: no danger words of its own (the generic screen is on); 'Safety steps, then go on' is off. Safety-rated boots: the shop says plainly in writing that the rating can't be promised after any repair, and the customer says yes first. Orthopedic or medical shoes: only the outer repair; the reason stays on the secure page. A sole or upper cracked through stops that part of the work (A8-35, B8-30): a written note and photo, nothing charged for what was not done. Adults book; a parent books a child's shoes; no child is left at the shop.
By name: a stitched resole is the master cobbler's work only, so the 'by name' branch stays on (A4-15, B4-16); other work goes to any cobbler.
Own steps: A8-x01 (the ticket: both shoes photographed, wear noted, READY date), B8-x01 (the shoes taken to the shop, signed for), B8-x02 (the return with a code, a try-on, then DONE). Words ops: A8-35, A10-23 (reminders at 30 and 60 days, a final written notice before the 90-day donation, the owner decides), A7-13, A7-70, B8-41 (DONE moved to the return day, shows the total), B8-47, S11-48.
Dates run forward: visit Thu Oct 22, shoes taken 9:30am (B8-x01), return Tue Oct 27 8:15am (B8-x02), DONE 9:00am (B8-41, time words op). The tailor's own-step dates were not copied.
Not built: mail-in repairs, orthotics, shoe shine on the spot, bag-only jobs as their own kind of work.
Known master limits (see the log): hard-coded 'haircut' words in A4-14, A4-42, A5-05, A6-14 on the visit and deposit paths; the S1-13 owner replies and read-backs; S12-09 / S12-10 price the second service at the first one's price; S12-19 and S11-99 license steps are not gated by the plug-in.
